Rashi on Yevamot 2b:10:1.hebrew: ור"ש היא - דאמר בפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין מט:) שריפה חמורה, ולהכי תנא רישא בתו ובת בתו — כולהו עד אם חמיו — בשריפה:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:10:1.english: And it is [according to] Rabbi Shimon - For he said in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 49b) that [execution by] burning is [more] severe [than stoning], and therefore he taught at the beginning [of the Mishnah] his daughter and his daughter's daughter — all of them through his father-in-law's mother — [as they are punishable] by burning.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:11:1.english: With regard to his mother-in-law it is written - “And if a man takes a woman and her mother, it is depravity; they shall be burned with fire” (Leviticus 20:14).

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:11:2.hebrew: כלתו - בסקילה בפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נג.), וכל שאר עריות דמתני' אינן במיתת בית דין אלא בכרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:11:2.english: His daughter-in-law - [Is punishable] by stoning, [as stated] in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 53a); and all the other forbidden relations of our Mishnah are not [punishable] by court execution, but rather by *karet* [excision].

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:12:1.hebrew: כיון דאתיא מדרשא - ליאסר עליו — חביבא ליה לתנא, ואקדמה ברישא. ולקמן מפרשי לה:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:12:1.english: Since she is derived from an exposition - To be forbidden to him — she is dear to the Tanna, and he taught her first. And later [the Gemara] explains it.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:1:1.hebrew: ואשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו - כגון ראובן שמת בלא בנים, ונולד לו אח לאחר מיתה ושמו לוי, ועמד שמעון וייבם אשתו, ולו אשה אחרת, ומת בלא בנים, ונפלו שתיהן לפני לוי — שתיהן פטורות. לפי שאשת ראובן שנשאת לשמעון אסורה ללוי, וענוש כרת עליה, לפי שאשת אח בכרת כשאר עריות שבפרשה, דכתיב בכולהו: "כי כל אשר יעשה מכל התועבות האלה ונכרתו". ובמקום מצות יבום, כשמת בלא בנים, שריה רחמנא; ואשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, שמת קודם לידתו, לא שרא ליה, דכתיב: "כי ישבו אחים יחדיו" — שהיתה להם ישיבה אחת בעולם. והלכך, משמת ראובן נאסרה על לוי איסור עולם כאשת אח שיש לה בנים; ואפילו עכשיו שנפלה לפניו מכח נשואי אחיו שמעון שהיה בעולמו, אסורה לו בשביל ראובן. וכשם שהיא אסורה לו, כך צרתה — אשת שמעון האחרת — אסורה, דילפינן לקמן על כל העריות העומדות עליו בכרת שנפלו לפניו לייבום עם צרותיהן, ששתיהן פטורות. ואם נשאן, ענוש כרת, שמאחר שפטרן הכתוב, עומדות עליו באיסור אשת אח שיש לו בנים:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:1:1.english: And the wife of his brother who was not in his world - For example, Reuven died without children, and a brother was born to him after [his] death whose name was Levi. And Shimon arose and took his [Reuven's] wife in levirate marriage, and [Shimon] had another wife; and [Shimon] died without children, and both of them fell before Levi [for levirate marriage] — both of them are exempt. Because Reuven's wife, who was married to Shimon, is forbidden to Levi, and one incurs *karet* [excision] for [cohabiting with] her, because [the prohibition against marrying] a brother's wife carries *karet*, like the other forbidden relations in the passage, as it is written concerning all of them: "For whoever shall commit any of these abominations, even the souls that commit them shall be cut off" (Leviticus 18:29). And in the case of the mitzvah of levirate marriage, when [a brother] died without children, the Merciful One permitted her; but [in the case of] the wife of his brother who was not in his world, who died prior to his birth, He did not permit her to him, as it is written: "When brothers dwell together" (Deuteronomy 25:5) — [meaning] that they had a shared dwelling in the world [i.e., their lifetimes overlapped]. And therefore, once Reuven died, she was forbidden to Levi with a permanent prohibition, like a brother's wife who has children; and even now that she falls before him by virtue of the marriage of his brother Shimon, who was in his world, she is forbidden to him on account of Reuven. And just as she is forbidden to him, so too her rival wife — Shimon's other wife — is forbidden, as we learn below concerning all forbidden relations whose prohibition carries *karet* that fall before him for levirate marriage along with their rival wives, that both of them are exempt. And if he married them, he incurs *karet*, for since Scripture has exempted them, they remain [forbidden] to him under the prohibition of a brother's wife who has children.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:1:2.hebrew: וכלתו - שמת בנו, ונשא אחיו כלתו — אסורה לו לעולם, ואפילו לאחר מיתת בנו:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:1:2.english: And his daughter-in-law - [In a case where] his son died and his brother married his daughter-in-law — she is forbidden to him forever, and even after the death of his son.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:2:1.hebrew: וכולן שמתו - שמתה בתו קודם לאחיו, או מיאנה. והיכי משכחת לה מיאון בבתו, והרי הוא קיים, ואין מיאון אלא ביתומה? משכחת לה, כגון שאביה השיאה לה לאחד ונתגרשה כשהיא קטנה, ושוב אין לאביה רשות בה, והלכה ונשאת לאחיו בעודה קטנה ויצאה במיאון. ובפ' ב"ש (לקמן יבמות קט.) קרי לה יתומה בחיי האב. ואם נתגרשה מאחיו, או מיאנה באחיו, או נמצאת אילונית — שמקחו מקח טעות, ולא הויא אשת אחיו — וכשמת אחיו, הרי היא כמו שאינו אשתו, ומתייבמת צרתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:2:1.english: And all of them who died - [That is,] where his daughter died before his brother [died], or she refused [him]. And how can you find [a case of] refusal with his daughter? For behold, he is alive, and refusal applies only to an orphan [girl]! You can find it, for example, where her father married her off to someone and she was divorced while she was a minor, and her father no longer had authority over her, and she went and married his brother while she was still a minor, and exited [the marriage] through refusal. And in the chapter [entitled] "Beit Shammai" (below, Yevamot 109a), it calls her "an orphan in the lifetime of the father." And if she was divorced from his brother, or refused his brother, or was found to be an aylonit — for his acquisition was an erroneous transaction, and she was not his brother's wife — and when his brother died, behold, she is as though she were not his wife, and her co-wife enters levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:4:1.hebrew: ואי אתה יכול לומר כו' - שכבר ילדו מאחר קודם שנישאו לאחיו, הלכך לאו אילונית היא. ומיאון נמי ליכא, שהרי גדולות הן, ואין ממאנת אלא יתומה קטנה, כדמפרש לקמן בפ' ב"ש:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:4:1.english: And you cannot say, etc. - For they had already given birth from another [man] before they married his brother; therefore, she is not an aylonit. And refusal [mi'un] also does not apply, for behold, they are adults, and only a minor orphan [girl] can refuse, as is explained below in the chapter [entitled] "Beit Shammai".

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:5:1.hebrew: כשם שבתו פטורה - שהרי אסורה לו, ואין שם אח אלא הוא — כך צרתה פטורה, כדיליף בגמרא:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:5:1.english: Just as his daughter is exempt - For she is forbidden to him, and there is no brother there other than him — so too, her rival wife is exempt, as is derived in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:5:2.hebrew: הלכה צרת בתו ונשאת לאחיו השני - דהיכא דיש אח אחר ששתיהן מותרות לו, אינן פטורות, שהרי יש כאן מצות יבום, ומתייבמת האחת, והשניה פטורה, דכתיב: "את בית אחיו" (דברים כ״ה:ט׳) — בית אחד הוא בונה, ולא שתים. ואם ייבם האחד את צרת בתו, ולו אשה אחרת, ומת בלא בנים, וחזרו ונפלו לפניו:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:5:2.english: His daughter's rival wife went and married his second brother - For where there is another brother to whom both of them are permitted, they are not exempt, as there is a mitzvah of levirate marriage here; and one [of them] enters into levirate marriage while the second is exempt, as it is written: "...his brother's house" (Deuteronomy 25:9) — one house he builds, but not two. And if that [brother] took his daughter's rival wife in levirate marriage, and he had another wife, and he died without children, and they returned and fell before him [the father].

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:5:3.hebrew: כשם שצרת בתו פטורה - שנאסרה עליו משעת נפילת אחיו הראשון, שנפלה עם בתו לפניו ופטרתה בתו הימנו. והרי היא עליו כאשת אח שיש לו בנים, ואסורה לו עולמית:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:5:3.english: Just as his daughter's rival wife is exempt - For she was forbidden to him from the time of the falling [to levirate marriage upon the death] of his first brother, when she fell before him together with his daughter and his daughter exempted her from him. And behold, she is to him like the wife of a brother who has children, and is forbidden to him forever.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:5:4.hebrew: כך צרת צרתה - אשת אחיו השני האחרת פטורה, שזו פוטרתה. וטעמא יליף בגמרא מלצרור (ויקרא יח), שצרת ערוה פוטרת צרתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:5:4.english: So too the rival wife of her rival wife - The second brother's other wife is exempt, because this one exempts her. And the Gemara derives the reason from "to be a rival" (Leviticus 18:18), that the rival wife of a forbidden relation exempts her [own] rival wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:6:1.hebrew: ואפי' הם ק' - אחים. והלכה צרת צרתה של בתו ונתייבמה לאחיו השלישי, ולו אשה אחרת, ומת בלא בנים — שתיהן נאסרות על זה, וכן לעולם:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:6:1.english: Even if they are one hundred - [Meaning] brothers. And [if] the rival wife of his daughter's rival wife went and was taken in levirate marriage by his third brother, and he had another wife, and he died without children — both of them are forbidden to this [first brother], and so on, forever.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:7:1.hebrew: צרתה מותרת - להתייבם לו, שהרי בשעת זיקת ייבום אינה צרתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:7:1.english: Her rival wife is permitted - To enter into levirate marriage with him, for at the time of the levirate bond, she is not her rival wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:8:1.hebrew: וכל היכולה למאן - כגון שהערוה קטנה ויכולה למאן ולא מיאנה, ומת אחיו — הואיל וקידושיה אינה אלא מדרבנן, וזיקת נפילתה מדרבנן, אינה פוטרת צרתה מן החליצה; ולהתייבם אסורה, כדמפרש טעמא בגמרא, שנראית צרת ערוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 2b:8:1.english: And any [woman] who is able to refuse - For example, where the forbidden relative was a minor who was able to refuse, and she did not refuse, and his [the yavam's] brother died — since her betrothal is only Rabbinic, and the levirate bond of her falling [for levirate marriage] is Rabbinic, she does not exempt her rival wife from ḥalitza; and [the rival wife] is forbidden to enter into levirate marriage, as the Gemara explains the reason: that she appears to be the rival wife of a forbidden relative.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:9:1.english: Now, all of them - [This refers to] the forbidden relatives, in that they are exempt from levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 2b:9:2.english: We derive [them] from a wife's sister - [This is explained] later in our discussion.

Tosafot on Yevamot 2b:11:1.hebrew: דלבתר שריפה סקילה חמורה - בחנם נקט הכי, דאפילו היתה סקילה קלה בכל ד' מיתות בית דין — ה"ל למיתני כלתו בתר חמותו; דבכל הנך ליכא מיתה אלא כרת לחודיה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 2b:11:1.english: "For after burning, stoning is severe" - [The Gemara] stated this unnecessarily, for even if stoning were the least severe of all four court-imposed death penalties, [the Tanna] should have taught [the case of] his daughter-in-law after his mother-in-law, as in all those other [cases] there is no death penalty, but only karet alone.

Tosafot on Yevamot 2b:12:1.hebrew: בתו כיון דאתיא מדרשא חביבא ליה - היינו בתו מאנוסתו, כדפי' בקונטרס; אבל בתו מנשואתו — מ"ערות אשה ובתה" נפקא, דלא גרע מבת אשתו. וא"ת: והיכי נפקא? והא אין מזהירין מן הדין, כדאמר לקמן בפ"ב (דף כב:) גבי "אחותך בת אביך (היא) או בת אמך", דצריך למכתב "אחותך היא" לחייב על אחותו בת אביו ובת אמו, לומר שאין מזהירין מן הדין! ואר"י: דלא דמי; דהתם לא איירי קרא אלא באחותו שאינה מן האב ומן האם, ד"בת אביך או בת אמך" משמע מן האב שלא מן האם ומן האם שלא מן האב, וכדמפרש קרא בהדיא: "מולדת בית או מולדת חוץ" (ויקרא י״ח:ט׳), דמתרגמינן: "דילידא מן אבוך מן איתתא אוחרת, או מן אמך מן גבר אוחרא". ואע"ג דדרשינן (לקמן יבמות כג.): "מולדת בית וגו'" — בין שאומרים לאביך קיים בין שאומרים לאביך הוצא, מ"מ אין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו; ואם היא בת שניהם — מק"ו הוא דילפת. אבל בכלל "אשה ובתה" הוי שפיר בת שהיא בת אשתו, כדאשכחן בפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין נג.) דאמו שהיא אשת אביו הויא בכלל אשת אביו. ובת אשתו, היכא דנכנסה לחופה ולא נבעלה — נראה לר"י דחייב על בתה, אע"ג ד"ערות אשה ובתה לא תגלה" כתיב, דמשמע ביאה; דסברא הוא דאין תלוי בביאה, דהא לא מיחייב על בת אנוסתו, אלמא בקידושין תליא מלתא, ואין סברא לומר דבתרוייהו תליא מלתא. והא דלא מיחייב על בת אנוסתו, כמו שפי' בקונטרס — משום ד"אשה ובתה" כתיב, דמשמע לשון אישות, מדלא כתב "אם ובת". ומיהו בהדיא בריש נושאין על האנוסה (לקמן יבמות ד' צז.) מפרש הש"ס טעמא אחרינא: דעריות "שאר" כתיב בהו — בנשואין איכא שאר, באונסין ליכא שאר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 2b:12:1.english: His daughter, since [the prohibition] is derived from a homiletical interpretation, is dear to him - This refers to his daughter from a woman he raped, as explained in the Kuntres [Rashi]. But his daughter from his married wife is derived from [the verse], "The nakedness of a woman and her daughter [you shall not uncover]" (Leviticus 18:17), for she is no worse than [any other] daughter of his wife. And if you say: And how is she derived [from there]? But [isn't there a rule that] we do not administer a warning based on a logical deduction [din]? As [the Gemara] says below in the second chapter (22b) regarding [the verse]: "[The nakedness of] your sister, the daughter of your father (she is) or the daughter of your mother" (Leviticus 18:9) — that it was necessary to write: "she is your sister" (Leviticus 18:11) to hold [one] liable for his sister who is [both] the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother, to state that we do not administer a warning based on a logical deduction! And the Ri says that it is not comparable. For there, the verse speaks only of his sister who is not from [both] the father and the mother, as "the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother" implies: from the father and not from the mother, or from the mother and not from the father; and as the verse explicitly explains: "born at home or born abroad" (Leviticus 18:9), which we translate [in the Targum]: "who was born of your father from another woman, or of your mother from another man." And even though we interpret homiletically (below, Yevamot 23a): "'born at home...' — whether they say to your father, 'Keep [her],' or whether they say to your father, 'Send [her] out'" — nevertheless, a verse does not depart from its plain meaning; and if she is the daughter of both of them, it is [only] by an a fortiori inference (kal va-chomer) that you would derive it. However, within the category of "a woman and her daughter," a daughter [of his] who is the daughter of his wife is fully included, just as we find in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 53a) that one's mother who is the wife of his father is included in [the prohibition of] "the wife of his father." And as for the daughter of his wife in a case where she [the wife] entered the bridal canopy (chuppah) but had not had intercourse, it appears to the Ri that he is liable for her daughter, even though it is written: "The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover," which implies intercourse [with the mother]; for reason dictates that it does not depend on intercourse, for he is not liable for the daughter of a woman he raped. Thus, the matter depends on betrothal (kiddushin), and it is not reasonable to say that the matter depends on both [marriage and intercourse]. And that which he is not liable for the daughter of a woman he raped, as explained in the Kuntres, is because it is written: "a woman and her daughter," which connotes the language of marriage [ishut], since it did not write "a mother and daughter." However, explicitly at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Nos’in Al HaAnusah (below, Yevamot 97a), the Talmud explains another reason: that regarding forbidden relations, "kinship" [she'er] is written concerning them — through marriage there is kinship, [whereas] through rape there is no kinship.

Tosafot on Yevamot 2b:3:1.hebrew: או שנמצאו אילונית - דאילונית קדושי טעות הן, ולא היתה אשת אחיו. ותימה, [דאמרינן] (לקמן יבמות ד' סא:): קטן וקטנה לא חולצין ולא מייבמין כו', קטנה שמא תמצא אילונית — ואמאי? תתייבם ממה נפשך: דאם אינה אילונית — שפיר מייבם, ואם היא אילונית — נמי שרי, דלא היתה אשת אחיו! ואר"ת, דההיא בקבלה עילויה; וכה"ג משני בריש בן סורר (סנהדרין סט:). וה"ר אברהם מבורגויילה תירץ: בנמצאת אילונית בחיי האח והקפיד, אבל לאחר מיתה — דלמא אם היה קיים לא היה מקפיד. ולא נהירא, דבהדיא קתני בתוספתא (פ"א): נמצאו אילונית, בין בחיי הבעל בין לאחר מיתה — צרותיהן מותרות. ובגמ' אפרש בע"ה: למאן דשרי צרת בתו אילונית אפי' בהכיר בה, מאי חידוש השמיענו בתוספתא "בין מחיים בין אחר מיתה"? וא"ת: דהכא משמע דאילונית לא בעי גט [אפי' מדרבנן], דאי בעיא — היתה צרתה חולצת ולא מתייבמת, כדתנן במתני': "כל שיכולה למאן ולא מיאנה כו'". ובכתובות בפרק אלמנה (דף ק:) תנן: "הממאנת והשניה והאילונית אין להם כתובה" — משמע: הא גיטא בעיא, דהכי דייק בהמדיר (כתובות דף עג. ושם)! וי"ל: דהתם נקט האי לישנא משום דלא מצי למנקט "אינן צריכין גט" משום שניה דקתני בהדייהו; תדע, דע"כ ממאנת לא בעיא גיטא. א"נ, בהמדיר לא דייק הכי אלא משום דברישא קתני "אינה מקודשת" ובסיפא "תצא שלא בכתובה". והא דתנן בהשולח (גיטין דף מו: ושם): "המוציא אשתו משום אילונית לא יחזיר", ומפרש משום קלקולא, דשמא תנשא לאחר ויהיה לה בנים ויאמר כו' ונמצא גט בטל ובניה ממזרים — דמשמע בעיא גט! אר"י: דהתם במוציאה משום ספק אילונית, שאין הסימנים ניכרים יפה; תדע, דקתני סיפא "נשאת לאחר והיו לה בנים", ואילו ודאי אילונית אין לה רפואה, דבהערל (לקמן יבמות עט:) פליגי ר"ע ור"א בסריס חמה אם חולץ וחולצין לאשתו, שיש לו רפואה, ובאילונית לא אשכחן דפליגי. אף על גב דבקידשה על תנאי וכנסה סתם איכא למ"ד בהמדיר (כתובות עב:) דבעיא גט — היינו דוקא בשאר מומין, דאיכא דמחיל; אבל אילונית, שום אדם אין מוחל. ואפי' לאביי דמפרש טעמא משום דאין אדם בועל בעילת זנות — היינו בשאר מומין דמסיק אדעתיה, ובדעתו אפי' יהיו בה מומין בועל לשם קדושין; אבל אילונית דלא שכיח לא מסיק אדעתיה, ומשום חשש אילונית לא יהא בועל לשם קדושין:
Tosafot on Yevamot 2b:3:1.english: "Or if they were found to be an ailonit" - For [the marriage of] an ailonit is an erroneous betrothal, and she was [never] his brother's wife. And it is astonishing, [as we say] (below, Yevamot 61b): "A minor male and a minor female neither perform chalitzah nor enter yibbum, etc.; a minor female [does not enter yibbum because] perhaps she will be found to be an ailonit." But why? Let her enter yibbum whichever way you look at it: for if she is not an ailonit, he properly performs yibbum; and if she is an ailonit, [relations with her] are also permitted, for she was not his brother's wife! And Rabbeinu Tam answered that that [ruling] is where [the husband] accepted her upon himself [regardless of defect]; and a similar resolution is given at the beginning of [the chapter] Ben Sorer (Sanhedrin 69b). And Rabbi Avraham of Bourgueil answered: [Our Mishnah deals with a case] where she was found to be an ailonit during the brother's lifetime and he objected; but after [his] death, perhaps had he been alive he would not have objected. However, this is not plausible, for it is explicitly taught in the Tosefta (chapter 1): "[If] they were found to be an ailonit, whether during the lifetime of the husband or after [his] death, their co-wives are permitted." And in the Gemara I will explain, with God's help: According to the one who permits the co-wife of his daughter who is an ailonit even where he recognized [her condition], what novelty did the Tosefta teach us [by specifying] "whether during [his] lifetime or after death"? And if you say: Here [in our Mishnah] it implies that an ailonit does not require a get [even rabbinically], for if she required [a get], her co-wife would have to perform chalitzah and could not enter yibbum, as we learned in our Mishnah: "Anyone who is able to perform mi'un and did not perform mi'un [her co-wife performs chalitzah and does not enter yibbum]." Yet in Ketubot, in the chapter Almanah (100b), we learned: "A woman who performs mi'un, and a secondary forbidden relative [sheniyah], and an ailonit have no ketubah" — which implies that she does require a get, for this is how [the Gemara] infers in HaMaddir (Ketubot 73a and ibid.)! And one can say: There [in Ketubot 100b], it employed this phrasing because it could not state "they do not require a get" on account of the sheniyah taught alongside them; you may know [that this is so], for perforce a woman who performs mi'un does not require a get. Alternatively, in HaMaddir [the Gemara] did not infer this except because in the first clause it taught "she is not betrothed," whereas in the latter clause [it taught] "she leaves without a ketubah." And as for that which we learned in HaSholei'ach (Gittin 46b and ibid.): "One who divorces his wife on account of [her being] an ailonit may not remarry [her]," and [the Gemara] explains [that this restriction is] due to a potential pitfall — lest she marry another man and bear children, and he will say, etc., so the get would be found void and her children would be mamzerim — which implies that she requires a get! Rabbi Yitzchak [the Ri] said: There, it is where he divorces her because of uncertainty whether she is an ailonit, where the signs are not clearly discernible. You may know [this is so], for the latter clause teaches: "she married another and had children"; whereas a definite ailonit has no cure, for in [the chapter] HaArel (below, Yevamot 79b), Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Eliezer disagree regarding a congenital castrate [saris chamah] as to whether he performs chalitzah and whether his wife is subjected to chalitzah, because he has a cure, but regarding an ailonit we do not find that they disagree. Even though in [a case where] one betrothed her conditionally and then consummated the marriage without stipulation, there is an authority in HaMaddir (Ketubot 72b) who holds that she requires a get — that is specifically regarding other blemishes, which some people may overlook; but an ailonit, no person ever overlooks [such a defect]. And even according to Abaye, who explains the reason as being that a person does not engage in licentious intercourse — that applies to other blemishes, which enter his mind, and in his mind he engages in intercourse for the sake of betrothal even if she has blemishes; but an ailonit, which is uncommon, does not enter his mind, and on account of a concern for an ailonit he would not engage in intercourse for the sake of betrothal.

Tosafot on Yevamot 2b:4:1.hebrew: ואי אתה יכול לומר בחמותו שמיאנה - וא"ת: משכחת לה מיאון בקידושי טעות, דתנא דבי ר' ישמעאל: "אפי' בנה מורכב על כתיפה — ממאנת והולכת לה"? ותירץ ריב"ן, דמתני' איירי בקטנות. ועוד אמר ר"י, דבקדושי טעות מצי למימר דאפי' מיאון אינה צריכה, ולא הוה מצי למיתני בסיפא "כל שיכולה למאן" כו'. וממאנת דר' ישמעאל — לאו דוקא, דאפי' לא מיאנה לאו אשתו היא, ואם ערוה היא — צרתה מותרת. מיהו, בפרק בא סימן (נדה נב. ושם) משמע דבקדושי קטנות [נמי] איירי ר' ישמעאל, גבי בתו של ר' ישמעאל שבאת למאן בבית המדרש ובנה מורכב על כתיפה, ורבתה בכיה בבית המדרש, ואמרו: "דבר שאמר אותו צדיק יכשל בו זרעו?!", ונמנו וגמרו: "עד מתי הבת ממאנת? עד שתביא ב' שערות". ומשום ר' ישמעאל קאמר דנמנו, דליכא למימר משום דר' יהודה נמנו, דאמר "עד שירבה השחור על הלבן", דהא מודה רבי יהודה בנבעלת דאינה יכולה למאן. והא דפריך בפרק נושאין על האנוסה (לקמן יבמות ק: ושם): "וממאנת, מי קא ילדה?", ומשני: "בקדושי טעות, כר' ישמעאל" — הא דשביק קידושי קטנות דאיירי בהו, לאו משום דמודי ר' ישמעאל בקידושי קטנות, אלא משום דההיא סוגיא אליבא דשמואל, ושמואל לא סבר לה כרבי ישמעאל בקדושי קטנות, כדמוכח בפרק מי שמת (ב"ב קנו: ושם), אבל בקדושי טעות סבר כוותיה, כדאמר בהמדיר (כתובות עד. ושם): "קידש על תנאי ובעלה — אינה צריכה הימנו גט", והיינו כרבי ישמעאל. וצריך לומר: מתני' — לא כרבי ישמעאל. והא דקאמר בגמרא (דף ט.) "בפלוגתא לא קמיירי" — היינו דוקא אמנינא דט"ו נשים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 2b:4:1.english: "And you cannot say with regard to his mother-in-law that she refused" - And if you say: You can find [a case of] refusal with a mistaken betrothal, for the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: "Even if her son is riding on her shoulder, she refuses and goes on her way"? And the Rivan resolved that our Mishnah is dealing with [the refusal of] minor girls. And furthermore, the Ri said that in [a case of] a mistaken betrothal, one can say that she does not even require refusal, and [the Mishnah] could not have taught in the concluding clause: "Anyone who is able to refuse..." etc. And [the expression] "she refuses" of Rabbi Yishmael is not exact, for even if she did not refuse, she is not his wife, and if she is an ervah, her rival-wife is permitted. However, in the chapter [entitled] "Ba Siman" (Niddah 52a and there), it implies that Rabbi Yishmael is [also] dealing with the betrothal of a minor girl, regarding the incident of the daughter of Rabbi Yishmael, who came to refuse in the study hall while her son was riding on her shoulder, and weeping multiplied in the study hall, and they said: "A matter that that righteous man stated, should his offspring stumble in it?!", and they took a vote and concluded: "Until when may a daughter refuse? Until she develops two hairs." And [the Gemara] states that they took a vote on account of Rabbi Yishmael, for one cannot say that they took a vote on account of Rabbi Yehudah, who said "until the black [hair] exceeds the white," as Rabbi Yehudah concedes that once she has engaged in intercourse, she cannot refuse. And as for that which [the Gemara] challenges in the chapter [entitled] "Nos'in Al HaAnusah" (below, Yevamot 100b and there): "Can a woman who refuses give birth?", and answers: "In [a case of] a mistaken betrothal, in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael" — that [the Gemara] set aside the betrothal of a minor girl, which [Rabbi Yishmael] also dealt with, is not because Rabbi Yishmael concedes regarding the betrothal of a minor girl; rather, because that sugya is according to Shmuel, and Shmuel does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael regarding the betrothal of a minor girl, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] "Mi SheMet" (Bava Batra 156b and there), but regarding a mistaken betrothal, he holds like him, as [Shmuel] says in [the chapter entitled] "HaMaddir" (Ketubot 74a and there): "If one betrothed conditionally and engaged in intercourse, she does not require a bill of divorce from him," and this is in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael. And one must say: Our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael. And as for that which [the Gemara] says in the Gemara (page 9a), "It does not deal with [matters of] dispute" — that was stated specifically regarding the tally of the fifteen women.
